output:
**What I found.** The subject is a proposed `StorageProvider` interface wrapping your only S3 client. Reject it for now (the record calls this DROP), and the fact that decides it is the one you stated yourself: there is no second storage vendor named, planned, or requested. That is the "generality without instantiation" category — a strategy with one strategy. It fails the necessity gate before any cost/benefit scoring, so I did not score value or cost.

**Why it matters.** Acting on the proposal buys an interface that must be designed against exactly one implementation, which means it will encode S3's semantics anyway (keys, multipart, presigned URLs, consistency, error taxonomy) and will not actually fit the hypothetical second vendor when one appears. Not acting costs you nothing recoverable: if a real second store is ever named, extracting the interface then is a mechanical refactor with the second implementation in hand to shape it — cheaper and more accurate than guessing now. The one genuine need in this area is a test seam, and that is a different obligation with a much smaller mechanism.

**Do this first.**
1. Keep calling the S3 client directly; if the calls are scattered, consolidate them into one internal module (e.g. `storage.*`) that owns credentials, key naming, and retry — a module, not an interface with one implementor.
2. If tests need to avoid real S3, stub at that module's functions or use a local S3-compatible fake; don't introduce a vendor-portability abstraction to get a test double.
3. Write the rejection down (one line in your ADR or issue tracker) so it isn't re-proposed without a named second vendor.

**What I did not check.** I inspected nothing — `grep -ri "s3|S3Client|boto3|aws-sdk|StorageProvider"` over `.` returned no files, so this verdict rests entirely on your description. Re-run that grep in the real repo to confirm there is genuinely one call site cluster and no half-built abstraction already present. I also did not check for a compliance or contractual requirement for data portability/multi-region egress (§8c floor) — if one exists, it changes the answer, and nothing in what you told me suggests it does.

```
Subject:        Proposed StorageProvider interface in front of the sole S3 client
Mode:           Prospective
Necessity:      Fail
Necessity note: §1a "Generality without instantiation" — abstraction whose anticipated
                variation has no instance: one implementation, no second vendor named,
                planned, or requested. §8a optionality premium does not apply: it
                requires a named, probable next feature; speculative portability is
                exactly the case YAGNI nullifies.
Outcome evidence: none
Decision:       DROP (necessity failure)
Rationale:      The problem the interface solves — swapping storage vendors — does not
                occur in this stack today and no source names it as forthcoming. An
                interface designed against a single implementation will mirror S3's own
                semantics and is unlikely to fit a real second vendor, so it buys
                indirection now and re-work later. Extraction with a second
                implementation in hand is strictly better-informed than extraction now.
Next action:    Stop. Call the S3 client directly; if call sites are scattered,
                consolidate into one internal storage module (no interface) and record
                the rejection.
Verification:   Not run — grep for s3/S3Client/boto3/aws-sdk/StorageProvider over the
                working directory returned no files; verdict rests on stated facts.
Minimal alt:    A single internal storage module owning credentials, key naming, and
                retry, stubbed directly in tests. Captures the testability and
                consistency value without the portability abstraction.
Reopen when:    A second store is named with an owner and a date (vendor migration,
                on-prem/air-gapped deployment, regional residency requirement), or a
                contractual/regulatory data-portability obligation is mapped to this
                code path. Then extract the interface from the two concrete clients.
```
